messages:
alice: seeing repeated tail-latency spikes on eu-west pool-p-5 since last night. 95th/99th token latency jumps ~3-5x for some tenants. Not correlating with GPU utilisation (stays ~30-40%).
ben: same. telemetry shows NIC egress queues saturating, and kernel backlog spikes. looks like bursts from a few high-egress tenants are coupling into shared qdiscs.
carmen: devops-bot dropped an alert at 03:12 UTC: `pool-p-5: tail_latency=420ms, gpu_idle_pct=65%` — bot log attached in thread.
devops-bot: ALERT: pool-p-5 egress-queue-depth > 1024 packets for 6min; affected slices: tenant-phi, tenant-orchid.
adelaide (ops): pinging net team, could be driver-level transmit queue coupling across VF.
dinesh: interesting that GPU is idle while NIC is busy — suggests I/O-blocked tasks waiting on reads/writes. Could be file-shim or model cache thrash. any cache-miss patterns?
alice: cache miss rate increased for those tenants but not enough to explain the magnitude. I/O microbursts line up with client-side batching changes that rolled yesterday.
eva: quick reproducer: run a steady small-req qps on many tenants + one tenant with 5x bigger embedding pushes and you can see egress qdepth climb and other tenant RTTs spike.
ben: idea list: 1) per-tenant egress shaping (tc + fq_codel + tbf), 2) SR-IOV isolate heavy tenants to separate VF, 3) scheduler-level backpressure detect and avoid assigning new sequences to NIC-bound tasks, 4) dedicate egress lanes for Dedicated pools. tradeoffs: perf vs cost.
carmen: can we try a lightweight eBPF policer first? cheap, cluster-side, non-disruptive. scope: target top 2% sinks by egress bytes.
dinesh: agree. eBPF ring policer should cap burst and preserve fairness. I can prototype a map keyed by tenant-id from xdp.
alice: prototype tc command that mitigates in host namespace (example):
``` 
# attach per-tenant classful qdisc
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 10gbit
# tenant class (burst cap)
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:100 htb rate 1gbit burst 50kb
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 100 fw flowid 1:100
```
ben: nice. but htb on host is heavy at scale — we need kernel-bypass-friendly approach for latency-sensitive tails. eBPF + samples seems better.
eva: I'll run the eBPF prototype in staging on pool-p-5a for tenant-orchid and tenant-phi. expected rollout: 2h test then measure 95/99 percentiles.
carmen: also put a temporary routing rule: route heavy-egress tenants to dedicated slice group that has isolated NIC VF. that reduces cross-tenant coupling while we tune policer.
dinesh: note: isolating by VF will increase infra cost ~+12% in eu-west due to underutilised NIC lanes. need a customer-impact note.
alice: call with support later today to flag affected tenants. we should offer to move them to dedicated slices temporarily (ops-assisted) and explain latency vs cost.
besides (ops): small checklist: deploy eBPF policer, enable tc rule fallback, run synthetic regression, collect p99 token latency and kernel tx-queue depth histograms.
eva: staging run started 04:18 UTC. i'll post results in ~90m.
ben: long term: scheduler change to include 'egress_pressure' score per node so we can bias allocation away from nodes with active bursts. that will reduce need for per-tenant hardware isolation.
dinesh: also think about KV cache prefetching for embedding-heavy tenants to reduce egress. cheaper than adding NIC lanes.
alice: action items: dinesh prototyping eBPF policer (owner: dinesh), eva staging run + metrics (owner: eva), ben to draft scheduler egress_score proposal (owner: ben), carmen to coordinate support comms (owner: carmen).
carmen: adding to backlog and notifying account teams. :white_check_mark:
ben: will also model cost delta for VF carveouts — need numbers by EOD.
alice: thanks all. anyone see any regression on other pools? not yet. keep eyes open and post noisy tenants to this thread. :eyes:
